A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWE-Perf study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of ten oracle-setting LLMs and two repository-level systems, together with runtime measurements and analyses of their optimization performance.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and additionally reports runtime variability and the distribution of optimization strategies among benchmark instances.

M1.justification: The five-phase benchmark pipeline is retained, but its written procedure is corrected: Section 3.2 changes the performance-gain filter from below 0.3 to above 0.3, and Algorithm 1 swaps the original/modified runtime inputs while retaining the test expression. These are localized procedural corrections; the PDFs do not establish that collection or scoring was rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions use 140 instances from the same nine repositories and retain the Oracle file-level and Realistic repository-level tasks. Appendix B.3 classifies existing instances by optimization strategy without adding evaluated datasets, languages or scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same ten oracle LLMs, expert reference, and Agentless and OpenHands comparisons using Claude-3.7-sonnet. Reordering the realistic-setting rows and correcting a plotted Qwen label do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix C.1 changes OpenHands' maximum iterations from 50 to 2,000, a fortyfold revision to its stated inference budget. The filtering inequality and Algorithm 1 runtime orientation also change the documented selection/scoring protocol. These are reported protocol revisions; unchanged result tables do not establish whether experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.3 analyzes benchmark representativeness through four optimization-strategy categories. Existing correctness-conditioned, target-function-count, runtime and word-cloud analyses remain. Appendix B.1 explains threshold choices but does not add a threshold sensitivity experiment.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 first reports timing variability through an average coefficient of variation of 10.976%. Algorithm 1 also corrects which runtime distribution is adjusted and compared. The three screening runs, twenty verification measurements and significance level of 0.1 remain unchanged; additional runs are not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds the 10.976% runtime coefficient of variation and strategy proportions: redundancy elimination 25.7%, algorithmic logic 26.4%, data/resource optimization 15.0%, and cache/compatibility 32.9%. Existing table scores and matched performance-plot values remain unchanged, including OpenHands' 2.26% and the expert's 10.85% in Table 2. The changed stated budget prevents interpreting these as a same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes A from original to modified runtimes and B from modified to original runtimes. With B_adj = B × (1 − x) and the greater-sided Mann–Whitney test unchanged, this corrects the mathematical direction of the minimum-gain calculation rather than merely renaming variables. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty claim, data-collection and evaluation contributions, and substantial model–expert performance-gap claim. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds noise-versus-cost explanations for threshold choices, while B.3 interprets strategy diversity and explicitly identifies concentration in Python repositories. Section 3.1 changes its future-work recommendation from omitting performance-related tests to omitting target functions. Existing result interpretations and the limitation that expert patches may be suboptimal remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 revises the OpenHands iteration limit while retaining model identifiers, other decoding settings, hardware and the oracle prompt. v2 removes the project homepage link and the academic-license/use-restriction disclosure from v1's safeguards section. Its new Impact Statement instead reports public release of tasks, tools and results, without a replacement project-access link.

R1.justification: v2 adds CodeEditorBench (Guo et al., 2024) to the introduction and PIE (Shypula et al., 2024) to related work. Existing positioning against function-level benchmarks and GSO remains. Consolidating duplicate SWE-Lancer entries does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, corrects the oracle-prompt cross-reference, swaps the runtime and target-function analysis subsections, and subdivides Appendix B. It replaces the template acknowledgment with an Impact Statement and updates author/contact information. Most prose and the overall scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a colored single-column template to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figures 5 and 6 exchange numbers, Figures 7–9 are grouped horizontally, and Table 2 changes row order and emphasis. Figure 2's target labels and the final model label in the correct-only performance plot are corrected. All fourteen figures and five tables remain.

improvement.justification: Correcting the gain-filter direction and Algorithm 1's runtime roles resolves concrete contradictions in the benchmark specification. The added noise estimate, threshold rationale and strategy analysis also improve methodological clarity and dataset characterization. These gains are limited by the unexplained 50-to-2,000 iteration-budget revision alongside unchanged scores and the removal of the project-access link; the revision does not establish stronger empirical performance.
